text:
Lane Hutson plays almost 25 minutes a night for Montreal, more than anyone, and the Canadiens take 57% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) when he's out there, 11.5 points better than without him. That's the number that tells you who he is. TSN's Montreal 690 called him the best player on the ice recently, and on a team whose results are leaning on its goalie, Hutson is one of the few Habs actually winning his minutes.

The points are fair: 18 in 20 games, 15 of them assists, with his goals right on his expected total. There's no luck to give back here and no drought to wait out. Our talent range has him around 74 points.

The Calder winner from 2024-25 was Evolving-Hockey's top defenseman by wins above replacement last season, 1st among 215, with 99th-percentile play-driving and a knack for drawing penalties. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries. Our model's closest comparisons are Charlie McAvoy and Adam Fox. With Mike Matheson hurt, expect his minutes to climb again.
